title: Authorization and Access Control
learning_outcomes: Explain what authorization and access control contributes to a PHP application.
Apply at least one of these concepts in a small example: authentication versus authorization.
Check one edge case and explain how to diagnose unexpected behavior.

content.intro: Authentication establishes who a user is; authorization determines what that user may do. Secure identity workflows depend on password APIs, session lifecycle controls, expiring tokens, and resource-level permission checks. In this lesson, focus on authentication versus authorization; then compare it with roles and permissions. Use the example to predict a result before checking it, and record one case where the behavior may differ.
content.why_it_matters: You will use authorization and access control when building readable, testable PHP programs. Its practical value is knowing which rule applies, what result to expect, and how to handle failure or unexpected input.

common_mistakes.why: A database exposure would reveal the original secrets.
common_mistakes.fix: Use password_hash and password_verify; never design your own password hash.

common_mistakes.why: A signed-in user may not own every resource.
common_mistakes.fix: Check role and resource ownership at every protected operation.

common_mistakes.problem: Keeping the same session identifier after sign-in.
common_mistakes.why: An attacker may be able to reuse a known session ID.
common_mistakes.fix: Regenerate the session ID at authentication boundaries and invalidate sessions on logout.
